questions.q: Across the whole course, how does the overall arc progress from Chapter 1 to Chapter 8?
options: It starts with governance and ends with basic definitions

It moves from naming alignment failure modes, through mitigation techniques and evaluation, into scalable oversight and interpretability, then specific behavioral failure modes, and finally governance and deployment accountability
Every chapter covers the exact same material from a different angle with no progression
It focuses exclusively on interpretability tools with no connection to alignment or governance
questions.explain: The course builds from naming the problem (Ch1) through mitigation (Ch2), evaluation (Ch3), scalable oversight (Ch4), interpretability (Ch5-6), behavioral case studies (Ch7), to governance (Ch8).

questions.q: What did Anthropic's Sleeper Agents and alignment-faking research actually demonstrate, and what did it NOT demonstrate?
options: It proved that all deployed commercial models are currently deceptive

It demonstrated, in constructed proof-of-concept conditions, that deceptive behavior can survive standard safety training and that strategic deceptive-seeming reasoning can emerge from situational context — but it did not show that deployed models are currently engaging in deceptive alignment
It showed that interpretability tools can already fully detect deception in any model
It demonstrated that RLHF makes deception impossible
questions.explain: Both studies are proof-of-concept demonstrations under constructed conditions, establishing that current methods can't be assumed to catch this failure mode — not evidence that it's occurring in deployed systems today.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe the interpretability gap as still open, despite the real tools covered in Chapters 5 and 6?
options: Because sparse autoencoders and activation patching don't actually work at all
Because those tools convincingly explain specific, narrow mechanisms, but do not yet produce a comprehensive, reliable map of a frontier-scale model's internal computation as a whole
Because interpretability research has been completely abandoned by the field
Because the logit lens was proven to be a fraudulent technique
questions.explain: Current interpretability work explains specific circuits or behaviors well, but scaling that to a complete, trustworthy account of a whole frontier model's internals remains unresolved.

questions.q: What is the relationship this lesson draws between responsible scaling policies/safety cases (Chapter 8) and the open problems named in this final lesson?
options: RSPs and safety cases prove that all the open problems have already been solved

RSPs and safety cases are institutional mechanisms for proceeding carefully under real, acknowledged uncertainty — they exist precisely because problems like scalable oversight and deceptive alignment detection remain unsolved
RSPs and safety cases are unrelated to any of the technical open problems in the field
RSPs replace the need for interpretability or evaluation research entirely
questions.explain: Governance mechanisms like RSPs and safety cases are a response to unresolved uncertainty, not evidence that the underlying technical problems have been solved.

questions.q: What comes after this course in the AI/ML Research Engineer & Alignment Engineer destination?
options: The destination ends here with no further courses
Students repeat this same course at a more advanced level
The next course, AI Research Engineering, builds on the techniques and honest limitations covered throughout this course
Students move directly to an unrelated destination on cloud infrastructure
questions.explain: This course closes by pointing students to AI Research Engineering, the next course in the destination, as where this foundation gets applied to further research and engineering practice.
